title: Unify-store: Terraform provisioner for EBS/EFS/S3 with snapshot sanity + upgrade path
creator: Maya Chen
description: Goal: deliver a single, opinionated Terraform provisioner that standardizes EBS, EFS, and S3 bucket provisioning for Private (VPC) deployments. The provisioning layer should enforce encryption-by-default (KMS), sane snapshot lifecycles, tagging and ownership metadata, and provide a lightweight health-verifier that surfaces snapshot/capacity anomalies to Console. The module must provide a clear upgrade path from existing customer TF state (v1 -> v2), opt-in compatibility flags, and documented migration steps.
acceptance_criteria: Terraform module (registry-style) creates EBS volumes, EFS filesystems, and S3 buckets with KMS CMKs or customer-supplied KMS key IDs
Default snapshot lifecycle policy applied for EBS/EFS and lifecycle rule for S3 backups, configurable TTL and retention
Module emits CloudWatch metrics and a Lambda-based health verifier that runs daily and reports to a metrics namespace + CloudWatch alarm
Upgrade flag `v1_compatibility` allows older attribute names for 3 months with a deprecation warning in Terraform plan
Automated tests (terratest) for creation, update, and destroy in a CI stage and a sample private-deploy example in examples/
Documentation and migration guide published to Confluence and linked in module README

implementation_notes: Module layout: /modules/unify-store with submodules ebs/, efs/, s3/ and common/ for kms/key-management, tagging, and lifecycle policies
Defaults: encryption = true (KMS CMK), snapshot_retention_days = 30, s3_backup_ttl_days = 90

Health verifier: Lambda (Go) triggered daily via EventBridge; checks snapshots last-modified, EFS per-filesystem used_percent, and S3 incomplete-multipart jobs; publishes metrics and writes an incident-style event to an SNS topic for on-call routing
Upgrade strategy: add computed shim attributes for legacy names, emit plan warning, provide `migrate_state` helper script to move state names in-place using `terraform state mv` examples
Testing: terratest matrix for aws account scaffold using ephemeral test VPCs in CI; add a light-weight acceptance job in release pipeline (private-acceptance)
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: KMS key policy edge-cases for cross-account snapshot copy could expose keys. Mitigation: default to customer-managed CMK and include strict policy template with least-privilege cross-account statements; require explicit opt-in for cross-account copies.

Risk: Large snapshot retention increases customer costs. Mitigation: sensible default retention (30d), clear documentation of cost trade-offs, and an automated retention report in Console during rollout.
Risk: Backwards compatibility could increase maintenance burden. Mitigation: time-box `v1_compatibility` to 3 months and include migration tooling in PR
